newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.02-3.12 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.02-3.12 percent.

text.p: German call money rates were little changed on Wednesday at around 3.02 percent to 3.12 percent despite the Bundesbank's 4.1 billion mark drain from the banking system earlier in the morning.
A drain of a couple billion marks had been expected.
Traders said the Bundesbank's decision to allocate 74 billion marks was aimed at returning allocations to normal levels after several large offerings were made last year to even out cash flows.
Traders said call rates could slip a bit as banks park funds not used at the Bund auction at midday.
Banks held 42.4 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Tuesday, up from 40.5 billion marks the day before. The average for the month now stands at 41 billion marks.
Banks borrowed only about 100 million marks from the emergency Lombard lending facility.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was quoted at 3.09492 percent on Wednesday compared with 3.09925 percent the day before.
